title: Home as an orchestrator on a built project's chat: a team of specialists, follow-ups that act, tables from the app, a task board
request: Not really helpful: the home agent must be more intelligent and have other agents to do multiple tasks, an orchestrator with a multi-agent team. Start with the fixes and the orchestrator, then the task board and specialists, and use the budget to test it in a real situation. It must reach every part of the app: asked about the best model it should bring the models table.
spec: A built project's chat matched keywords: 'ok do it' and 'ok' got a stage-explain answer with no facts, 'build improvements' got the advice again, and the improvement job had failed with no word in the chat.
plan: Step 0: follow-ups carry out the pending offer, 'improvements' is understood, a failed job is said, no answer from empty facts
Step 1: an orchestrator that reads the conversation and the project's state, planned by the model (home_orchestrator) with the rules as fallback
Step 2: specialists as tools of a new registry scope 'home' (Records reader, Evaluator, Experimenter, Notebook coder), cards with tables in the chat, a task board that follows a job
Live test on a scratch copy of the owner's real project, the screenshot's conversation first, capped spend

decisions.decision: Specialists are registry tools of one scope, not separate model agents.
decisions.why: One harness, one guard and one capture for every move; the model plans, deterministic code reads the records and runs the jobs.

decisions.decision: A reply's sentence with a number no tool returned is dropped.
decisions.why: The model never computes a score; a table card is the truth and the text may only cite it.

decisions.decision: An offer answers the next message only.
decisions.why: The review found a 'thanks' two turns later started an improvement run.

decisions.decision: The live test runs on a file-workspace copy of the project with jobs recorded, not run.
decisions.why: A real situation without changing the owner's project; the full job path was then checked separately with a scratch worker.

decisions.decision: Writes are refused while the project runs something.
decisions.why: A job saves the project as it runs; a write then can lose its update or leave it marked running.

change: draft/orchestrator.py (new: Turn, 12 read tools and 3 write tools in scope 'home', HomeGuard, rules plan, grounded(), Orchestrator with model and rules turns, task board, watcher, kept turns), prompts/home_orchestrator.md (new), draft/chat.py (reply_built delegates), draft/api.py, agents/{__init__,harness,registry}.py and prompts/__init__.py (the scope and the agents home.project, home.project.rules), models/settings.py (purpose home_orchestrator), web: views/home.html (project cards, task board, notebook cell with Run, chips, light Markdown), core.js (board events), look.css; tests/test_home_orchestrator.py (new), test_agent_harness.py, test_model_data_limits.py, test_built_chat.py; scripts/home_orchestrator_live.py (new).

findings.defect: 'ok do it' and 'ok' got nonsense; 'build improvements' got advice again.
findings.scenario: After 'improve the model for me' the person said ok.
findings.cause: Keyword regexes with no memory of the chat's offer; the fallback asked a stage-explain prompt with no facts; 'improve' did not match 'improvements'.
findings.fix: The orchestrator reads the conversation (model) or the pending offer (rules); IMPROVE matches every form of the word.

findings.defect: The improvement job failed with 'no handler for jobs of kind improve' and nothing was said.
findings.scenario: The owner's improve request on the dev app.
findings.cause: An orphan worker from the morning, on old code, claimed the job; the chat had no follow-up of jobs.
findings.fix: The orphan was stopped; a task board follows each job and says a failure with its reason and a hint to restart.

findings.defect: Live run 1: the model started a second improvement run on 'ok'.
findings.cause: The state shown to the model did not say a run was queued.
findings.fix: working_now in the state; improve_model refuses while a run is queued or running.

findings.defect: Correct sentences about the confusion counts were dropped.
findings.scenario: 'It flagged 13, 6 were right' on the evaluation.
findings.cause: The totals were not in the card.
findings.fix: Flagged, actual positives and actual negatives added to the evaluation card.

findings.defect: Replies lost their lines and showed **bold** as text; fit times shown with 4 decimals.
findings.scenario: The models answer in the browser.
findings.cause: grounded() rejoined sentences with spaces; no Markdown on the page; one number format.
findings.fix: Lines kept; mdLite (escaped first); per-column digits.

findings.defect: The board stayed 'running' on the page after the job ended.
findings.scenario: A real improvement job on the scratch copy.
findings.cause: The page's event stream listened to a fixed list of kinds without 'board'.
findings.test: browser check: running to done live

findings.defect: A stale offer started an improvement run.
findings.scenario: 'How can it improve?', 'show the evaluation', 'great, thanks'.
findings.cause: The offer was cleared only by improve_model or a no.
findings.fix: The offer is read once at a turn's start and cleared; a tool offering again sets it again.

findings.defect: 'What did you try to improve?' gave the ideas and set an offer.
findings.scenario: After adding three tools at the head of WORDS.
findings.cause: WORDS[:1] pointed at the wrong entry.

findings.defect: A model failure after a write ran the write again and flipped the job's task to failed.
findings.scenario: The second request hits the cap after improve_model ran.
findings.cause: The rules replanned the same text; Turn.task overwrote the job's task.
findings.fix: After tools ran, the reply says what they did; a later failure is its own task.

findings.defect: The watcher thread read the default workspace's job store.
findings.scenario: A chat in a second workspace.
findings.cause: The services proxy reads a ContextVar that threads do not copy.
findings.fix: The thread runs in a copy of the request's context.

findings.defect: Adopt ran while an improvement job ran.
findings.cause: The guard did not check the project's running state.
findings.fix: HomeGuard refuses writes while the project runs something, and adopt while a run is queued.

findings.defect: An error's text and free-text activity payloads could reach the model.
findings.scenario: A provider error echoing the request; a person's words in an activity payload.
findings.fix: Only the error's type; activity shows known keys only.

findings.defect: The reply listed the models as text instead of a table.
findings.scenario: Asked which models were trained, the chat wrote a numbered list of families and scores.
findings.cause: The old answer had no cards; the model also repeated a shown table as a list.
findings.fix: The models come as a table card; beside a card, list lines are dropped and the words are capped at four sentences (the whole reply kept in the record).

outcome: On a built project's chat, Home understands follow-ups, shows the app's records as tables, improves the model, writes and runs notebook cells, and follows long jobs on a board that says how they ended.
lessons: Two workers on one queue: the stale one fails jobs it does not know. Check the processes before blaming the code.
A pending offer must expire: an acceptance word much later is not an acceptance.
A test that scripts a model per client restarts its script each turn: share one script, or the test passes for the wrong reason.
An event the page does not subscribe to never arrives: a new event kind needs its listener.
risks: The understanding agents (problem analyst, solution planner) are not yet in the built chat; a changed problem is not detected.
The prompt-hash check fails until make agent-eval and make harness-eval run for the new prompt and scope.
